title: Safety and efficacy of riboflavin-assisted collagen cross-linking of cornea in progressive keratoconus patients: A prospective study in North East India

groups.description: One eye (allocated by coin toss) of each of 39 patients with bilateral progressive keratoconus (age criterion 15-50 years, Kmax not above 60 D, CCT above 400 um); epithelium-off Dresden CXL, riboflavin 0.1% in 20% dextran for 30 minutes, UVA 365 nm at 3 mW/cm2 for 30 minutes; prospective parallel-group study (CTRI REF/2018/05/020083)
The fellow eye of the same 39 patients, allocated by coin toss before follow-up as the control eye; no cross-linking during the 6-month follow-up (artificial tear drops only)

notes: Fellow-eye design: the untreated control eyes were allocated before follow-up by coin toss and declared as the control group, so they are kept as an observation group.
Roles: the Dresden protocol is a standard treatment and the control eyes are observation; neither is an investigational agent, device or protocol, so both groups are role control.
Age group unstated: the age criterion is 15-50 years and only the mean age 23.795 +/- 5.44 years is reported, without a range.
Disease progression was recorded as an adverse event in the control group; the article does not report treatment of control eyes within the 6-month follow-up.
Table 1 also gives K Min, Sim K, cylinder, sphere, spherical equivalent, BCVA, UCVA, contrast sensitivity, IOP, endothelial cell count and hexagonality; Table 2 gives adverse events (not extracted).
